Munson Ridge SNOTEL (MSOA2) reported 12 inches of snow between midnight on the 21st and midnight on the 22nd, with a storm total amount of 18 inches. The Upper Chena SNOTEL (UCEA2)reported 9 inches of snow between the 21st and 22nd, with a storm total amounts of 13 inches.
Heavy snow fell across the Chatanika River Valley. The Little Chena Ridge SNOTEL (LCRA2) reported an increase in snow depth of 12 inches in 24 hours.
Heavy snow fell across the Upper Kobuk Valleys. The Dahl Creek SNOTEL (DHLA2) reported 9 inches of snow in less than 24 hours.

Winds increased across the Seward Peninsula during the morning hours of October 20th, by early afternoon winds were gusting above 50 mph, the strongest winds lasted a little over an hour at Nome (PAOM), where a peak gust of 58 mph was recorded. These strong winds destroyed a smokehouse, caused roof damage, and also knocked down power lines.

Widespread coastal flooding was reported across the Yukon Delta coast as strong winds pushed water onshore. A tribal official from Kotlik reported water flooding and lifting boardwalks, as well as extensive road flooding throughout the community, that closed the Kotlik Tribal Office. In Emmonak, 6 boats sank near the village. A tribal official from Nunam Iqua reported flooding. In Alaknuk, bank to bank flooding was reported.

events.cz_name: EASTERN NORTON SOUND AND NULATO HILLS
events.event_narrative: Widespread coastal flooding was reported across the eastern Norton Sound coast as strong winds pushed water onshore. Officials from Elim reported that Moses Point Road had logs and debris and had to be cleared. The creek was also backed up and had to be cleared to let the creek drain. In Koyuk, ice piled up to 3 feet in some areas and some fish racks were bent. In Shaktoolik, officials reported a loss of an unknown amount of shoreline protection berm and power outages. In Unalakleet, the airport power had to be shut down due to the impact of waves on their system (7.5 feet). High water was reported on the backside of town, as well a lot of debris was reported on roads that had to be cleared. High water eroded the area used for airport snow removal as well. In St. Michael, officials reported a derelict barge broke free, floated by the storm with concern of impacting fuel tanks. Stebbins reported minor erosion and debris.

Coastal flooding was reported along the southern Seward Peninsula coast as strong winds pushed water onshore. The City of Nome reported debris and erosion at mile 25 on the Nome Council Highway, the roads was rendered impassable at mile 24, and three sections required urgent attention, mile 16.5, mile 21 just past the bridge, and mile 24.5 at the breach. In Golovin, a spotter reported that the old airport runway was completely submerged.
Minor coastal flooding was reported in Gambell as waves washed over the runway deposited debris. The airport closed due to the debris on the runway.
Coastal flooding was reported along the Bering Strait coast as strong winds pushed water onshore. Teller officials reported that the Teller Road was under water.

Widespread coastal flooding was reported across Diomede and Shishmaref as strong winds pushed water onshore. Diomede lost power and Alaska Energy Authority (AEA) was engaged. Two shipping containers were floated by the storm. Tribal elders in Shishmaref reported the worst high water in memory. Severe shoreline erosion was reported on the north and south end of town. The village's protective berm was damaged.  Roads and the landfill were damaged, an archeological site was lost due to erosion, one outbuilding floated. Graves were swept away.
Coastal flooding was reported on the northern Seward Peninsula as strong winds pushed water onshore. The village of Deering reported water over the runway and the road to the airport flooded.

Widespread coastal flooding was reported in Kotzebue as strong winds pushed water onshore.  One residence partially collapsed into the ocean and 3 residences were evacuated. Numerous residences flooded. Approximately 38 residents sheltered at the Maniilaq Health Center. The airport was closed due to 4 to 5 feet of water and ice over both runways. The east side of the village was under water with many roads impassable. The waste water system was impacted.

Winds increased during the  morning hours of November 5th, with gusts reaching 60 mph. Falling snow in conjunction with the strong winds resulted in blizzard conditions at Point Thompson (PAAD), where visibility dropped below a quarter of a mile.

Winds increased across the Western Arctic Coast during the early morning hours of November 20th, gusting above 60 mph. Peak wind gusts of 64 mph were reported at Point Lay. Alaska DHS and EM, as well open source media reported wind gusts up to 70 mph at Point Hope that knocked out power to 80% of Point Hope and surrounding areas.

Winds increased along the Chukchi Sea coast during the early morning hours of November 19th, with frequent gusts of 60 mph or greater. Winds gusts to 77 mph were reported at Red Dog Dock (RDDA2) and to 60 mph at Kivalina (PAVL).
Blizzard conditions developed at Kotzebue (PAOT) during the early afternoon hours of November 19th. Winds gusted as high at 53 mph while visibility dropped below a quarter of a mile.

High winds developed during the overnight hours of November 18th and continued into the morning of November 19th. Winds at Teller (PATE) gusted as high as 66 mph, while at Wales (PAIW) wind gusts to 73 mph.
Winds increased in the Central Brooks Range during the morning of November 20th. Winds gusted as high as 65 mph at the Anaktuvuk Pass USARRAY (E22KX) site.
Blizzard conditions developed at Nuiqsut (PAQT) during the late morning hours of November 19th. Winds gusted as high at 46 mph while visibility dropped below a quarter of a mile.

Winds increased during the late evening hours of November 29th, with gusts reaching to 41 mph. This resulted in blizzard conditions at Point Thompson (PAAD), where visibility dropped below a quarter of a mile.
Strong southerly gap winds developed through Windy Pass and along the Parks Highway. Winds gusted as high as 79 mph throughout the event at the Antler Creek RWIS sensor.

events.cz_name: EASTERN ALASKA RANGE NORTH OF TRIMS CAMP
events.event_narrative: Southerly gap winds developed through Isabel Pass reaching speeds of up to 82 mph at the US Army Fort Greely Air Force Tower weather station. The strong winds persisted for approximately 48 hours.
Blizzard conditions developed at Point Lay (PPIZ) during the early morning hours of December 9th. Winds gusted as high as 49 mph while visibility dropped below a quarter of a mile.

Winds increased during the evening hours of  December 11th, with gusts reaching 66 mph on the 12th of December. Blowing snow due to the strong winds resulted in blizzard conditions at Deadhorse (PASC), where visibility dropped below a quarter of a mile for an extended period of time that extended into the early morning hours of December 13th.

Steady snowfall combined with strong winds overnight to produce blizzard conditions at Atqasuk (PATQ) during the early morning hours of December 13th. These conditions persisted into the early afternoon before visibility improved above one quarter mile. East winds consistently gusted to around 40 mph during the blizzard.
Local DOT reported blizzard conditions near Ice Cut Hill along the Dalton Highway. Considerable blowing snow was reported along with northeast winds of 48 mph.
Local observers and trained spotters reported 12 inches of snow over a 24 hour period at Chena River Recreation Area.
Local spotter reports 11 inches of snow in 24 hours at Birch Lakes.

events.cz_name: EIELSON AIR FORCE BASE AND SALCHA
events.event_narrative: Local facebook post indicated 8 of new snow at Salcha. Eielson AFB reported 9 of snow in a 24 hour period.
Local spotter from Nenana Hills reported 9 inches of snow in 24 hours.
Local trained spotter reports 12 new snow in 24 hours at Pleasant Valley.
Numerous spotter reports across the Fairbanks metro area reported 8 to 15 inches of new snow in 24 hours. This includes 15 at Ester, 13 at North Pole, and 12 2 miles southwest of College.

Strong southerly winds reached the northern Bering coastline during the early morning hours of December 21st and continued into the late morning of December 22nd. Point Hope (PAPO) measured a max wind gust of 73 mph during the afternoon of the 21st.

Strong southerly winds developed over Saint Lawrence Island during the afternoon of December 21st and continued to remain very gusty all the way into December 24th. Gamble reported a numerous gusts in excess of 60 mph with a maximum gust on December 24th of 78 mph. The community of Savoonga experienced a freezing spray event with ice coating windows, buildings, and powerlines and poles. Many power outages were reported in Savoonga due to downed power lines and poles.
The Umiat Air Field RAWS (UMTA2) reported an air temperature of -48F and wind speeds of up to 7mph resulting in a wind chill value of -71F.

Strong north/northeast winds originated over the southeastern Chukchi Sea and continued southwards through the Bering strait.  The strong winds impacted the northern coast of St Lawrence Island throughout the day with winds consistently gusting over 60 mph throughout the day.
Strong northeast winds blowing along the northwest arctic coastline produced very strong winds with gusts as high as 62 mph at Point Hope.

Heavy snowfall continued through the morning hours with wind speeds increasing into the afternoon to create very low visibilities at Atigun Pass. A local observer reported near white out conditions and visibilities well below 1/4 miles several hours. The local Department of Transportation reported very difficult driving conditions along the Dalton Highway through the pass.
Strong southerly winds blew through Windy Pass reaching a top speed of 72 mph at ACRS2 (Antler Creek) observation tower.

events.cz_name: EASTERN ALASKA RANGE NORTH OF TRIMS CAMP
events.event_narrative: Strong gap winds developed through Isabel Pass during the overnight hours with wind speeds near Fort Greely at site OPFA2 peaking at 86 mph during the morning hours.
SNOTEL data from the Seward Peninsula at Paragon Creek reported total snowfall of 8 with additional light snow still falling.
Strong southerly winds through Isabel Pass emerged into the Delta Junction area with a station MGTA2 at the Fort Greely main gate seeing about an hour of wind gusts near 60 mph.

Observations from the Kotzebue ASOS and local NWS employee revealed heavy snow and high wind setting in early on the morning of the 17th. By afternoon blizzard conditions with wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph and visibilities around 1/4 mile prevailed for several hours.

Strong winds and heavy snowfall combined to bring Blizzard conditions to much of Saint Lawrence Island through the morning hours. Wind gusts of 35 mph or greater were reported by the GBXA2 AWOS while visual confirmation of extremely low visibilities were observed on the FAA webcam at Gambell.

events.cz_name: SOUTH SLOPES OF THE CENTRAL BROOKS RANGE
events.event_narrative: The Wiseman COOP observer reported 13.2 inches of new snow for the 24 hours ending at 8am on January 24th.
The Bettles Field SNOTEL reported 8 inches of snow in 24 hours.
The Atqasuk AWOW PATQ reported several hours of blizzard conditions with visibility as low as .13 mile and wind gusts as high as 55 mph.

Blizzard conditions developed during the morning hours at Utqiagvik with the PABR AWOS reporting visibility down to .25 miles and winds gusting to 68 mph. The ASOS stopped reporting during the event, but public reports supported the blizzard continuing into the afternoon hours.

Alaska DOT reported on their 511 site that an Avalanche occurred at mile 219 of the Parks Highway and was blocking traffic in all directions. DOT estimated that at least 6 feet of snow was covering the highway as a result of the avalanche.

events.cz_name: EASTERN ALASKA RANGE NORTH OF TRIMS CAMP
events.event_narrative: The Texas (TEXA2) mesonet site near Fort Greely reported a wind gust of 90 mph while the Air Force Tower (AFTA2) location gusted to 91 mph.
The COOP observer in Minchumina reported an accumulation of 1 inch of freezing rain followed by 6 inches of snowfall on top of the ice in a 24 hour period.

Snow changed to freezing rain at McGrath and continued for over 30 hours. There was .94 inches of freezing rain that fell in one 24 hour period with over an inch of freezing rain total during the event. the Innoko Lodge lost power and reported ice covered trees and power lines were down.

Alaska DOT reported on the 511 site that numerous avalanches had occurred through Atigun pass resulting in closure of the Dalton Highway. During the time of the event the Chandalar Shelf mesonet site was reporting several hours of 30 to 40 mph wind gusts leading to extra snow loading in the area.

events.cz_name: WHITE MOUNTAINS AND HIGH TERRAIN SOUTH OF THE YUKON RIVER
events.event_narrative: The Upper Nome Creek SNOWTEL reported warning level snowfall on both the 24th and 25th. Over the course of the event 33 inches of snow was recorded. Alaska DOT closed the Elliott Highway at Eagle Summit.

Winds gusted as high as 71 mph at Ft Greely (PABI) with other locations consistently experiencing wind gusts in excess of 50 mph for several hours. Numerous trees were downed as well as multiple power outages in and around Delta Junction. As many as 900 residents were without power as a result.

Alaska DOT reported Blizzard conditions through Windy Pass along the Parks Highway. DOT crews reported not being able to tell when the snow stopped due to the amount of blowing snow and poor visibility.

events.cz_name: EASTERN ALASKA RANGE SOUTH OF TRIMS CAMP
events.event_narrative: Alaska DOT closed the Richardson Highway from mile 186 to mile 218 due to very heavy snow and extremely low visibility in blowing snow. Snowfall totaled 6 inches and winds were estimated to have been between 60 and 70 mph.

The Chevak Airport AWOS (PAVA) reported Winter Storm conditions with visibilities dropping to between 1/4 and 1/2 mile for more than 12 hours while reporting heavy snow and fog. Sustained winds of 30 to 40 mph were common during this time frame.

The Savoonga AWOS (PASA) reported almost 10 hours of heavy snow and visibilities between 1/4 and 1/2 mile. Winds were sustained at 30 to 35 mph with gusts to 40 mph. On occasion visibilities dropped to below a quarter mile due to the blowing snow.
Selawik AWOS (PASK) reported a surface temperature of -36F and 18kt wind speed resulting in a wind chill of -70F.
Winds consistently gusted at or above 60 mph for approximately 18 hours with a peak gust of 77 mph registered at Cape Lisburne LRRS (PALU).
Winds consistently gusted at or above 50 mph for approximately 7 hours with a peak gust of 64 mph registered at Wales (PAIW).
Blizzard conditions prevailed for about 9 hours at Gambell where the local AWOS (PAGM) recorded 1/4 mile visibility and wind gusts between 45 mph and 50 mph.

Blizzard conditions began in the late evening and continued well into the night at Nuiqsut (PAQT). Observations consistently showed 40 mph winds gusts and visibility at around 1/4 mile. ASOS observations were lost overnight, but webcams provided visual reference that the blizzard conditions continued well into the night.

The Barter Island AWOS (PABR) reported near constant wind gusts of 45 mph to 50mph and visibilities fluctuating between 1/10th and 1/4th mild through the night as Blizzard conditions persisted. Heavy snow as also falling at the same time.

Barter Island experienced a short lived blizzard while heavy snow continued to fall. Winds gusted to around 40 mph for approximately 3 hours while the visibility dropped to 1/4 mile at Barter Island (PABA).

events.cz_name: WRN TANANA VLY WRN YUKON VLY
NE. SLOPES OF THE ERN AK RNG

events.event_narrative: NWS Employee in Nome reported steady freezing rain through the morning hours with .25 inch accumulation of ice at the noon observation. Roads were reported to be very slick with heavy ice accumulations on trees and power lines.

Strong east winds combined with heavy falling snow to produce blizzard conditions through the afternoon and into the night. Visibilities remained at or below 1/4 mile for an extended time period with wind gusts consistently at or above 40 mph at Nuiqsut (PAQT. Meanwhile at Deadhorse (PASC) winds gusted as high as 60 mph.

events.cz_name: WHITE MOUNTAINS AND HIGH TERRAIN SOUTH OF THE YUKON RIVER
events.event_narrative: Alaska DOT reported wind speeds of 43 mph and near zero visibility Over Eagle Summit. As a result the highway at Eagle Summit was closed for several hours until conditions improved.
Light snow combined with persistent strong northeast winds along the Northwest Arctic Coast to produce a short period of blizzard conditions at Point Lay (PPIZ).

Gusty winds combined with light snow during the early afternoon hours to reduce the visibility to 1/4 mile, resulting in blizzard conditions at Point Lay (PPIZ). These conditions persisted for the rest of the day.

events.cz_name: EASTERN NORTON SOUND AND NULATO HILLS
events.event_narrative: Strong north and northwest winds combined with periods of moderate snowfall to create an extended period of blizzard conditions. Wind gusts in excess of 35 mph and visibilities around 1/4 mile persisted for for almost 30 hours at Shaktoolik (PFSH).

PAVA reported winds greater than35 mph and visibilities of 1/4 mile or less from 4:40 PM to 8:20 PM on March 2nd. During the height of the blizzard, winds were sustained at 47 mph with gusts to 53 mph and visibility below 1/4 mile.

Blizzard conditions developed at PFKT (Brevig Mission Airport) prior to dawn and continued through midday. The visibility remained at or below 1/4 mile with falling snow and winds gusting as high as 63 mph.

The Kivalina AWOS (PAVL) reported winds in excess of 35 mph with gusts to 45 mph throughout the day. Heavy snow from the previous few days began to blow and the visibility remained at or below 1/4 mile for more than 8 hours.
The Nome (POAM) metar at 9:53 am reported 0.13 of ice. The Alaska State Troopers in Nome confirmed that there was a glaze of ice on cars, rails, and power lines.

A combination of steady snowfall and strong winds led to a period of visibilities reduced to or below one quarter mile at the Chevak AWOS (PAVA). During this time frame peak wind gusts were measured at 54 mph with gusts consistently between 45 and 50 mph.

Very strong gap winds developed through Windy Pass with the Antler Creek Mesonet (ACRA2) reporting wind gusts over 70 mph during the morning hours as strong southerly flow crossed the Alaska Range. A peak wind gust of 79 mph was recorded at 7:20 AM.

events.cz_name: EASTERN ALASKA RANGE NORTH OF TRIMS CAMP
events.event_narrative: Very strong gap winds developed through Isabel Pass with the Donnelley Dome Mesonet (K24KX) reporting wind gusts over 70 mph for almost 20 hours as strong southerly flow crossed the Alaska Range. A peak wind gust of 85 mph was recorded at 12:25 PM on the 16th.

Strong gap winds emerged out of Isabel Pass and crossed into the Tanana Valley near Delta Junction where the Delta Junction ASOS (PABI) reported a peak wind gust of 70 mph. Nearby mesonet site MGTA2 registered a maximum wind gust of 76 mph. Trees were reported down at Delta Junction and south of Greely. In addition social media showed a green house with the roof ripped off near Delta Junction.
Strong winds developed in the mid morning hours and eventually began gusting to between 35 and 45 mph creating blizzard conditions for over 12 hours at Point Lay (PPIZ).

The Wainwright ASOS (PAWI) reported blizzard conditions developing in the morning hours and continuing into the late evening. A peak wind gust of 49 mph was reported during the later stages of the blizzard.

Winds picked up resulting in blowing snow and blizzard conditions during the early morning at Barrow ASOS (PABR). Blizzard conditions persisted for almost 18 hours before visibilities increased. The peak wind recorded during the event was 45 mph.

The Deadhorse ASOS (PASC) reported blizzard conditions for approximately 12 hours with consistent wind gusts of 35 to 40 mph and visibilities at or below one quarter mile in blowing snow. The peak wind gust was reported to be 44 mph.

The Port Thompson AWOS (PAAD) reported the onset of blizzard conditions with winds gusting to 35 mph and visibilities in blowing snow of one quarter mile or less during the morning hours of the 16th. These condition lasted for over 48 hours as the east winds remain constant between 35 and 40 mph.

Blizzard conditions became established at the Chevak AWOS (PAVA) along the Yukon Coast during the early morning hours. These conditions persisted until midday with a peak wind gust of 48 mph reported.

PASC (Deadhorse) did not reach Blizzard Criteria and webcams showed much of the visibility reduction was due to fog and less so to blowing snow. However 511 reports (Alaska DOT) and blowing snow satellite products indicated blizzard conditions. 511 Report had peak wind of 52 mph, large snow drift near MM392 and visibility down to 1 delineator, approximately 500 feet.

Early morning 511 reports (Alaska DOT) and blowing snow satellite products indicated blizzard conditions. 511 Report had peak wind of 52 mph, large snow drift near MM392 and visibility down to 1 delineator, approximately 500 feet.

The Barter Island AWOS (PABA) reported Blizzard conditions with wind gusts as high as 40 mph and several hours of visibilities at or below 1/4 mile in blowing snow. While the event persisted for just over 24 hours, there were a few observations of up to 1/2 mile visibility at times during the overnight hours.
Trained Spotter reported more than 24 hours of steady snowfall with a 24 hour storm total snowfall of 8 inches at the top of Atigun Pass along the Dalton Highway.

Local social media reports from northeast of Fairbanks showed images of significant hail accumulation on the ground. One image did however picture one inch diameter hail near the intersection of Sheep Creek Road and Trilby Avenue.

AKDOT reported water overtopping roads and bridges throughout the area. As meltwater volume increased, major impacts followed including a significant washout at MP 315 on June 14th forced a four-day closure of the highway.

AKDOT reported extensive bank erosion and flooding from the Sag River along multiple stretches of the Dalton highway, with water overtopping roads and bridges throughout the area. As a result the Dalton highway was closed from Milepost 314-355.

events.cz_name: WRN TANANA VLY WRN YUKON VLY

events.event_narrative: Local social media reports indicated 1 inch diameter hail falling near Dot Lake and George Lake. Additional social media reports showed numerous hailstones collected along the Alaska Highway, but likely just under 1 inch in diameter.

events.cz_name: SOUTH SLOPES OF THE CENTRAL BROOKS RANGE
events.event_narrative: Public reports and photos delivered to the NWS River Forecast Center in Alaska indicated that the road to Wiseman was completely covered, thus preventing any travel into or out of Wiseman by automobile. It was estimated that the Middle Fork of the Koyukuk rose high enough to cover the road with water 18 inches deep.

Emergency management personnel with the Tanana Chiefs Conference and local officials from Allakaket reported a prolonged moderate to major flood that surrounded most of the lower community, Old Town, and the old runway. Several roads including the airport access road and Main Street washed out. The river officially crested at 64.54 feet on August 31st.

The Fort Greely/Big Delta ASOS reported a period of strong southerly winds through Isabel pass the persisted for just over 24 hours with sustained winds of 45 to 50 mph and consistent gusts to around 70 mph. The strongest gust occurred just prior to midnight on the 28th with a reading of 75 mph. There were reports on social media indicating that several trees were downed in and around Delta Junction as well as some minor roof damage.

Water over the Dalton Highway caused the road to wash out between mile markers 142 and 144 just north of Prospect Creek.  The Alaska DOT was forced to completely close the roadway between mile markers 112 and 156. All traffic was stopped at the Jim River DOT Camp.

events.cz_name: EASTERN ALASKA RANGE NORTH OF TRIMS CAMP
events.event_narrative: Strong Gap winds developed through Isabel Pass during the morning hours and peaked right around Noon. During this period sustained winds reported by the Texas Condo RAWS (TCOA2) were between 40 and 45 mph with gusts consistently in the 60 to 70 mph range.

events.cz_name: EASTERN NORTON SOUND AND NULATO HILLS
events.event_narrative: The Golovin AWOS (PAGL) reported strong southeasterly winds that persisted throughout the day, with sustained speeds of 50 to 55 mph and gusts around 65 mph. The strongest wind gust measured at the Golovin site was 68 mph on October 12th at 0714AKST. Further east, a peak gust of 76 mph was measured at the Shaktoolik AWOS site (PFSH) at 0856AKST. At the Elim Airport AWOS station (PFEL), a wind gust of 61 mph was measured at 0738AKST. Winds gusted to 81 mph at the St. Michael AWOS station (PAMK) at 0929AKST. A wind gust of 72 mph was recorded at the Unalakleet AWOS site (PAUN) at 1104AKST.||Reports obtained from social media included damage to the roofs and siding of multiple structures, including the Unalakleet Post Office. The porch and roof of one residential structure was destroyed. A fence was blown over. There were also reports of airborne debris.

The USArray fixed Vaisala WXT536 weather station, operated by the Alaska Earthquake Center on Kusilvak Mountain (K13KX), reported sustained winds of 45 to 75 mph from the night of October 11th through midday October 12th. A peak wind gust of 107 mph was measured on October 12th at 0554AKST. A wind gust of 66 mph was measured at the Emmonak AWOS site (PAEM) on October 12th at 0456AKST. At the Chevak Airport AWOS site (PAVA), a wind gust of 74 mph was recorded at 0543AKST on October 12th. The Kotlik Airport AWOS (PFKO) measured a wind gust of 81 mph at 0556AKST on October 12th.||At Kotlik, a house was blown from its pilings and came to rest on its roof. A power outage occurred after a utility pole was snapped.

The USArray fixed Vaisala WXT536 weather station, operated by the Alaska Earthquake Center at Tukpahlearik Creek (E18KX), reported sustained winds of 45 to 60 mph from the night of October 11th through the morning of October 12th. The peak wind gust of 87 mph was measured on October 12th at 0520AKST.
The Ralph Wien Memorial Airport ASOS (PAOT), located in Kotzebue, measured sustained winds of 44 mph and a peak wind gust of 59 mph on October 12th at 0611AKST.

A peak wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at the Kaiyuh Slough RAWS site (KAIA2) near Kaltag at 0921AKST on October 12th. The ASOS site at Galena (PAGA) reported numerous wind gusts exceeding 50 mph. Winds gusted to 71 mph at the USArray station (J19KX) in Poorman, 45 miles south Ruby. The Shaktoolik River RAWS station (SHKA2) recorded a wind gust of 93 mph at 0821AKST. The Nulato Airport AWOS (PANU) recorded a wind gust of 63 mph at 0751AKST.||In Koyukuk, high winds downed trees and caused a power outage. In Nulato, several trees were downed; trees fell on houses, sheds, and the post office. Roof and siding panels were peeled or ripped off structures.

events.cz_name: SOUTH SLOPES OF THE WESTERN BROOKS RANGE
events.event_narrative: The peak wind gust of 61 mph was recorded at the Imelyak RAWS site (IMYA2) near Ambler at 1139AKST on October 12th.
The Shungnak Airport AWOS (PAGH) measured a peak wind gust of 58 mph at 0455AKST on October 12th. Winds gusted to 58 mph on three separate occasions and exceeded 50 mph 18 times.

On October 12th at 1156AKST, the Huslia Airport AWOS (PAHL) measured a wind gust of 63 mph. Numerous gusts exceeding 50 mph were recorded at the station. Nearby, the Cottonwood Lake RAWS (COTA2) recorded multiple gusts in excess of 60 mph, with a peak gust of 64 mph measured at 1218AKST on October 12th.||Downed trees were reported in the community of Huslia, along with extensive damage to the roof of one structure.

The Shageluk Airport AWOS (PAHX) measured sustained south-southwest winds of 38 mph gusting to 52 mph at 0640AKST on October 12th. Peak winds were recorded at 0702AKST, with sustained speeds of 43 mph gusting to 66 mph. Twenty miles to the west, the Anvik Airport AWOS (PANV) measured a wind gust of 56 mph at 0525AKST. Thirty-two miles to the south-southeast of Anvik, the Holy Cross AWOS (PAHC) recorded a wind gust of 58 mph at 0502AKST. In the surrounding area, KSKO Radio reported that high winds downed numerous trees onto power lines, leaving many areas without power.

On October 11th at 2357AKST, the Reindeer River RAWS station (RDRA2), located 16 miles south-southeast of Pilot Station, recorded sustained winds of 37 mph gusting to 60 mph. Peak winds were recorded at 0557AKST on October 12th with sustained winds of 55 mph gusting to 86 mph. On October 12th at 0649AKST, the St. Mary's-Pitkas Point Airport AWOS (PASM) measured a wind gust of 76 mph. On October 12th at 0625AKST, the USArray fixed Vaisala WXT536 weather station operated by the Alaska Earthquake Center at Wolf Creek Mountain (K15KX), located 38 miles northeast of Russian Mission, recorded a wind gust of 79 mph. Wind damage was reported at Pilot Station and St. Mary's.

events.cz_name: EASTERN ALASKA RANGE NORTH OF TRIMS CAMP
events.event_narrative: The USArray fixed Vaisala WXT520 weather station operated by the Alaska Earthquake Center at Donnelly Dome (K24KX) reported sustained winds of 48 mph gusting to 71 mph at 0450AKST on October 12th. Peak winds occurred at 0955AKST with a gust of 81 mph.
On October 12th at 0810AKST, the Alaska Department of Transportation site located along Parks Highway at Antler Creek milepost 244 (ACRA2) reported a wind gust of 74 mph.
At 1700AKST on October 12th, an Alaska Department of Transportation webcam showed whiteout conditions at Atigan Pass.

A Facebook post from a resident of Kotlik at 0258AKST on October 12th indicated that a storage container was lifted and moved by high waters. At Scammon Bay, a member of the public reported minor flooding and a road washout via Facebook at 0602AKST on October 12th. At Emmonak, a member of the public reported high surf and a boat swept away at 1032AKST on October 12th. At Chevak, flooding was reported by a member of the public on October 12th.

events.cz_name: EASTERN NORTON SOUND AND NULATO HILLS
events.event_narrative: On October 12th, a mandatory evacuation order was given for Shaktoolik and parts of Elim.

The Anchorage Daily News posted an online article on their website stating a non-mandatory evacuation was issued at 13:30 local time on October 8th according to a Kivalina resident named Janet Mitchell. Later on October 8th, an online publication by KTUU AK News Source wrote a full evacuation was ordered for the city of Kivalina at 17:45 local time according to another Kivalina resident. In the October 9th AK SEOC SitRep, they documented 287 residents taking shelter overnight in the local gym on October 8th.

An emergency manager in Kotzebue received a report at 09:46 local time of water just shy of the road the city uses to trigger mandatory evacuation orders (the road name was not specified). Later that day, the City of Kotzebue issued a evacuation order at 12:05 local time advising residents in low-lying areas to seek shelter at the Kotzebue Middle/High School. That night, 103 people were successfully sheltered overnight and 6 residents were displaced. Additionally, the Kotzebue Sound Tide Gauge reported water levels at 5.74 ft at 17:00 local time on October 8th. In total, 52 homes sustained water damage and needed to be repaired.
Emergency managers reported at 15:00 local time on October 7th that boats were lost due to flood waters (caused by coastal flooding) inundating low-lying areas of the community.

The USARRAY mesonet (K13KX) located atop of Kusilvak Mountain reported an initial verifying observation of 53 kt peak wind at 11:45 local time on October 7th. The peak observation at this site was a 61 mph wind gust at 19:45 local time on October 7th. The hazard did not verify at lower observations due to winds not fully mixing down to the surface.

The DOT mesonet observation site (ACRA2) along the Parks Highway at Antler Creek (MP 244) reported an initial verifying observation of 70 mph wind gust at 23:00 local time on October 7th. An LSR was also sent on behalf of this observation under the classification of  Non-Thunderstorm Wind.

events.cz_name: EASTERN ALASKA RANGE NORTH OF TRIMS CAMP
events.event_narrative: The Air Force Tower mesonet (AFTA2) approx 13 mi SSW of Fort Greely reported an initial verifying observation of 72 mph wind gust at 12:40 local time on October 8th. An LSR was sent on behalf of this observation under the classification of Non-Thunderstorm Wind.

The Pilgrim Hot Springs SNOTEL site (PHSA2) located in the higher terrain of the southwestern Seward Peninsula experienced almost 48 hours of steady heavy snowfall. 8 inches of new snow was reported in the first 24 hours with a 48 hour total of 13 new snowfall.

Steady snowfall and persistent north winds of 35 mph gusting to near 50 mph at PAGM (Gambell) resulted in several hours visibilities dropping to or below 1/4 mile from the early afternoon hours of November 19th into the early morning hours of November 20th before the visibility finally began to improve.

Snowfall began at the Coal Creek SNOTEL (CLCA2) during the early afternoon of November 21st and continued through midday on November 22nd. The 24 hour snowfall total was 8 inches with 5 inches of that snowfall occurring in the first 6 hours of the event.

events.cz_name: WHITE MOUNTAINS AND HIGH TERRAIN SOUTH OF THE YUKON RIVER
events.event_narrative: The Upper Chena Dome SNOTEL (UCEA2) site reported a 24 hour total snow depth change of 9 inches from the early afternoon of November 21st into the early afternoon of November 22nd. The period of heaviest snowfall was between 6 AM and 8 AM on the 22nd when 3 inches of snow fell in a period of only 2 hours.

The Kotzebue ASOS station (PAOT) reported meeting blizzard criteria at 0953 on 12/11/25. There were multiple instances of blizzard conditions being met on and off between the hours of 1000 and 1100 on 12/22/25. Winds were consistently gusting up to 41 mph with visibilities as low as 1/4 miles.

The Teller Airport AWOS (PATE) reported meeting blizzard criteria at 0850 on 12/11/25. Heavy snowfall and low visibilities less than or equal to 1/4 miles were reported from the site between 0850 to 1335.

Blizzard criteria was met at the Nuiqsut ASOS (PAQT) at 0253 on 12/12/25 and continued for more than 3 continuous hours. Wind gusts were reported above 50 mph and with visibilities less than 1/4 miles. Additionally, the Deadhorse ASOS (PASC) also reported meeting blizzard criteria between the hours of 0825 and 1153 on 12/12/25, with peak wind gusts between 56 to 60 kts and visibilities less than 1/4 miles.

The Point Thomson AWOS (PAAD) reported meeting blizzard criteria at 0555 on 12/12/25 and continued through 0355 on 12/14/25. The AWOS site reported wind gust values above 60 mph and very low visibility less than 1/4 miles for more than 3 continuous hours.

The Atqasuk AWOS (PATQ) met blizzard criteria at 2245 on 12/11/25. Blizzard conditions continued for more than 3 continuous hours, but wind data was lost at 0355 on 12/12/25. The peak observation at PATQ was a peak wind gust of 55 mph with visibility less than 1/4 miles at 2050 on 12/11/25.

The Utqiagvik (Barrow) ASOS site (PABR) reported meeting blizzard criteria at 0550 on 12/12/25. Blizzard conditions were observed at the site between 0250 to 0845 on 12/12/25. A peak wind gust of 55 mph and visibility less than 1/4 miles was reported at 0640 on 12/12/25.
